BiblicalUsage: Raqach is to perfume, to compound ointment after the art of the apothecary. Moses was told to make the holy anointing oil, 'an ointment compounded after the art of the apothecary'; the incense was 'a perfume, a confection after the art of the apothecary, tempered together, pure and holy'; and the Preacher says dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour.
TheologicalSignificance: The lesson I take is that the perfumer's art is a picture of holiness: compounded pure, tempered together — and one dead fly is enough to spoil it.
